english: A man came to the house, who led ten sheep. The master was standing at the door. 'Give me your daughter!' 'What is the bride-price?' 'The bride-price is so many.' Then the master gave his daughter to him. They drank, and they rejoiced.

english: 'Mother, where is father?' 'He is in the cow-stall.' 'Make me sip!' 'Son, drink!' 'What are you weaving?' 'I am weaving wool.' 'I caught sight of a wolf!' 'Where did you catch sight of it?' 'I caught sight of it at the door.' 'Do not tremble at it! Sit down.'

pie: dwóh₁ gʷówh₁ gʷowsth₂ṓd h₁éǵʰs wédʰe. nu yungdʰí h₂érh₃trōy tóh₁. tóh₁ mē stunéds. tóh₁ wékʷesh₁ h₂éǵe. h₁yód tóh₁ ḱémh₂etes tóh₁ logʰéye. nu tóh₁ gʷowsth₂óm ǵʰidʰí.
english: Lead the two cattle out of the cow-stall. Join them to the plough. Do not hit them. Drive them with a word. When they are tired, make them lie down. Then drive them on to the cow-stall.

english: If a guest is standing at the door, stand up and go to the door. Lead him into the house. Give him wheat. Seat him at the table. Do not kill him. He is dear to the god. When it grows bright, let him go.

pie: (h₁)éḱwōs ewewkʷ, "ḱludʰí, h₂ówi! ḱḗrd h₂gʰnutoy widntbʰós: dʰǵʰémō(n), pótis, h₂wlnéh₂m h₂ówyom kʷnewti sébʰoy gʷʰérmom wéstrom; h₂éwibʰoskʷe h₂wlh₂néh₂ né h₁esti."
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

pie: h₂usési bʰudʰdʰí. nu ǵʰidʰí h₂éǵmn̥ h₁éǵʰs ḱwónm̥-kʷe ḱóm dukdʰí. ní mē légʰs. tód spéḱye tóm-kʷe ḱléwse. h₁yód wĺ̥kʷos gʷm̥yḗti HrudHdʰí úd. tóm gʷréwh₁ gʷʰn̥dʰí. nu h₂éǵmn̥ wéh₁ikom h₂éǵe. dyéw ph₂ter tód h₂léksoyh₁s.
english: Wake up at dawn. Drive the flock out. Lead the dog along beside you. Do not lie down. Look at it, and listen to him. If a wolf comes, cry out. Kill it with the spear. Then drive the flock into the enclosure. Father Sky, may you protect it!

pie: h₁r̥sḱétām bʰréh₂tēr swésōr-kʷe wódr̥ tód-kʷe dʰubʰnóm h₁ést. dʰǵʰúHes tósmi sn̥h₂ént. nu bʰréh₂tēr dʰǵʰúHm̥ gʷréwh₁ gʷʰént. nu pékʷet swésōr tóm. nu tóh₁ h₁dtā́m tóy-kʷe tetr̥pḗr. nu tóh₁ sísdetām.
english: The brother and the sister went to the water, and it was deep. The fish were swimming in it. Then the brother killed a fish with the spear. Then the sister cooked it. They ate, and they were satisfied. Then they sat down.

pie: kʷíd bʰréh₂ter ḱléwos h₁ésti? tód ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ h₁ésti. kʷésmōy ḱléwos h₁ésti? h₁yós h₂ŕ̥tḱom gʷʰénti h₁ésti méǵh₂ ḱléwos tósmey. h₂ŕ̥tḱom gʷʰéns? tóm gʷʰnént h₁nómn̥-kʷe moy ḱlutóm h₁ésti. h₁nómn̥ moy ḱlutóm h₁syéh₁t.
english: 'Brother, what is fame?' 'It is a famous name.' 'Who has fame?' 'He who slays the bear has great fame.' 'Did you slay a bear?' 'I slew it, and my name is known.' 'May my name be known!'

pie: ḱéywe h₂éǵmn̥ kúdʰe h₁ésti? tód dréwi Hn̥dʰí h₁ésti. wĺ̥kʷom dedórḱth₂e? dedórḱh₂e tóm wéh₁ikoy h₂énti. h₂éǵmn̥ péh₂somes. túH ḱunéh₁ ḱóm gʷh₂dʰí. h₁eǵ h₂én yéh₂mi. dyéw nos ph₂ter h₂lékse.
english: 'Dear one, where is the flock?' 'It is under the tree.' 'Have you seen the wolf?' 'I have seen it near the enclosure.' 'Let us guard the flock. You go with the dog. I go there.' 'Father Sky, protect us!'

pie: sléh₂gʷt méh₂tēr h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m nu tā́m uh₁inéHt. séh₂ dʰwóri sédyet. nu h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m tn̥nwn̥tíh₂ séh₂ tékst. h₁yód h₂éwsōs h₂wést swóm suHnúm téh₂eh₁ woséyet. méwdt só.
english: The mother took wool. Then she twisted it. She was sitting at the door. Then, stretching the wool, she wove. When Dawn grew bright, she clothed her son with it. He rejoiced.

pie: wéh₁ikom h₂usési gʷh₂tā́m. nu sddʰí h₂ówins ḱóm. úd mē HréwdHs. tā́s mē stunéds. téh₂bʰos bʰh₂dʰí. tā́s h₂ml̥ǵdʰí. bʰére bʰórom h₁n̥dóm.
english: At dawn go to the enclosure. Sit down beside the sheep. Do not cry out. Do not hit them. Speak to them. Milk them. Carry the load inside.

pie: owis eḱwōs kʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses

english: The wheat grew large. Then the father and the mother went to the field. He was cutting off the ears of grain, and she carried the load. The two sons dried the ears. Then they put the load on the wagon, and two swift horses pulled it. Then she crushed the wheat. Eating it, they rejoiced. 'Mother Earth, you gave us grain!'

pie: ḱéywe h₂ówim dedórḱth₂e? tā́m ne dedórḱh₂e. lelóykʷe séh₂. wĺ̥kʷos tā́m sléh₂gʷt? tód ne wóydh₂e. tā́m h₂isḱṓmes. gʷowsth₂óm ih₂dʰí h₁eǵ-kʷe dʰwórm̥ yéh₂mi. tā́m dréwi Hn̥dʰí widóm. séh₂ gʷíh₃weti? gʷíh₃weti séh₂.
english: 'Dear one, have you seen the sheep?' 'I have not seen her.' 'She is gone. Did the wolf take her?' 'I do not know that. Let us seek her. You go to the cow-stall, and I go to the door.' 'I found her under the tree!' 'Is she alive?' 'She is alive.'

pie: kʷís dʰwóri stestóh₂e? tr̥syónts gʰóstis h₁ésmi. srobʰéye me. wiḱdʰí h₁n̥dó. túH dʰh₁méns gʰóstipotis h₁ési? gʰóstipotis h₁ésmi. ní sddʰí puHróm-kʷe h₁ddʰí.
english: 'Who is standing at the door?' 'I am a thirsty stranger. Make me sip!' 'Come in!' 'Are you the master of the house?' 'I am the master.' 'Sit down and eat wheat!'

pie: h₁yód h₁regʷesyét stéh₂yet gʰóstis dwóh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁. nu wiHrós bʰéwdʰt tóh₁-kʷe ne kʷéḱt. súHnew bʰudʰdʰí. kʷís tóh₁ sléh₂gʷt? sléh₂gʷt só tóh₁. nu ḱwṓ tóh₁ séh₂gyet wiHrós-kʷe tóm sékʷeto. nu tóh₁ h₂én widónt. dedwóyth₂e só h₂epó-kʷe léytt. nu tóh₁ dʰéh₁mn̥ h₁élh₂t.
english: When it was getting dark, a stranger stole two horses. Then the man woke up and did not catch sight of them. 'Son, wake up! Who took them?' 'The stranger took them.' The dog tracked them, and the man followed it. There they saw them. The stranger was afraid, and he went away. Then he drove them home.

pie: léwkt h₂éwsōs nu h₂nḗr úd stéh₂t swóm-kʷe h₂éǵrom gʷéh₂t. dwóh₁ gʷówh₁ h₂érh₃trōy yungónts só tóh₁ h₂éǵet. nu h₂érh₃troh₁ h₂éryet h₁ést-kʷe sóh₂wl̥ bʰérǵʰont. swidyónts só ḱémh₂t. nu diwéy HréwdHt. dyéw moy ph₂ter h₂éǵrōy wódr̥ dh₃dʰí. dyḗws tóm ḱléwt h₂wérst-kʷe nébʰos-kʷe h₂epó léytt. h₁yód h₁regʷesyét tóh₁ dʰéh₁mn̥ wédʰet. nu suptós h₁ést.
english: Dawn grew bright. Then the man stood up and went to his own field. Joining the two cattle to the plough, he drove them. Then he ploughed with the plough, and the sun was high. Sweating, he grew tired. Then he cried out to Sky: 'Father Sky, give water to my field!' Father Sky heard him, and it rained, and the cloud went away. When it was getting dark, he led them to the house. Then he was asleep.

pie: puHróm pékʷye. nu wéǵʰe péh₂wr̥ dʰéh₁mn̥ wódr̥-kʷe tósmi dʰh₁dʰí. h₁yód tód yésēti tóm tósmi dʰdʰeh₁dʰí. stólom stn̥h₂dʰí. nu stóloy sísdete gʷr̥h₃éte-kʷe puHróm.
english: Crush the wheat. Carry fire into the house, and put water on it. When it boils, put the wheat into it. Set the table. Sit down at the table and eat wheat.

pie: h₁yód h₁regʷesyét sérpet wĺ̥kʷos wéh₁ikom. h₂éǵmn̥ tréset. ḱwṓ tóm ḱléwt só-kʷe HréwdHt. nu bʰéwdʰt h₂nḗr. nu swóm gʷéru h₁pónts só wĺ̥kʷom dʰwóri kʷéḱt. nu tóm tóh₁ moréyet. nu só h₂ew légʰt.
english: When it was getting dark, the wolf crept toward the enclosure. The flock trembled in fear. The dog heard it, and he cried out. Then the man woke up. Seizing his spear, he caught sight of the wolf at the door. Then he killed it. Then he lay down again.

pie: bʰuHyét nébʰos h₂wérst-kʷe. nu h₂óweyes trésont. h₂nḗr tā́s wéh₁ikom wédʰet. h₁éyt moysós pró téh₂es-kʷe sékʷonto. nu dʰwóri sédt. nu tód h₂wést h₁n̥dʰént-kʷe h₁éǵʰs.
english: A cloud was appearing, and it rained. The sheep trembled in fear. The man led them into the enclosure. The ram went ahead, and they followed. Then he sat down at the door. Then it grew bright, and they came out.

pie: túH gʷéru wérǵs? tód wérǵm̥. widé tód. tód dl̥h₁gʰóm h₁ésti tód-kʷe piḱróm h₁ésti. kʷíd toy dédeh₃mi? puHróm moy dh₃dʰí. puHróm h₂m̥bʰí dédeh₃mi. h₁opéyoyh₁t toy tód h₁wésuh₂ ḱléwos.
english: 'Did you make the spear?' 'I made it. Look at it!' 'It is long, and it is pointed. What am I giving you?' 'Give me wheat!' 'I give you wheat in exchange.' 'May it give you good fame!'

pie: swésor péh₂wr̥ dʰégʷʰeti? tód dʰégʷʰeti yéseti-kʷe wódr̥. bʰréh₂ter ǵr̥h₂nóm pékʷe. tód h₂réydʰoh₂. kʷís puHróm gʷr̥h₃éti? ḱwṓ gʷr̥h₃éti. tóm mē stunéds. h₁ésti só lewbʰós.
english: 'Sister, is the fire burning?' 'It is burning, and the water is boiling.' 'Brother, cook the grain!' 'I am preparing it.' 'Who is eating the wheat?' 'The dog is eating.' 'Do not hit him! He is dear.'

pie: h₁yód h₂éwsos léwkt wédʰet h₂nḗr gʷṓs gʷowsth₂ṓd h₁éǵʰs. nu h₂éǵrom h₁yént. tóy h₁dént tóy-kʷe píph₃ont. h₁yód sóh₂wl̥ bʰérǵʰont h₁ést sédt dréwi Hn̥dʰí. h₁yód h₁regʷesyét tóns gʷowsth₂óm ǵʰéyt. nu só suptós h₁ést ḱwṓ-kʷe tóns péh₂st.
english: When Dawn grew bright, the man led the cattle out of the cow-stall. Then they went to the pasture. They ate, and they drank. When the sun was high, he sat down under a tree. When it was getting dark, he drove them on to the cow-stall. Then he was asleep, and the dog guarded them.

pie: h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m moysṓd h₁pdʰí. h₂sowséye tā́m. nu tā́m uh₁inHdʰí tā́m-kʷe tn̥nudʰí. tā́m mē Hrunéps. tā́m pléḱte. woséyeso téh₂eh₁. h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ te gʷʰr̥nuyéh₁t.
english: Take wool from the ram. Dry it. Twist it, and stretch it. Do not break it. Weave it. Clothe yourself with it. May the wool warm you!

pie: wr̥ǵyét dʰugh₂tḗr h₂éǵroy. nu h₂ŕ̥tḱos dréwbʰos h₁nédʰt. nu séh₂ bʰebʰóyh₂e séh₂-kʷe HréwdHt. nu ḱléwt tósyeh₂s bʰréh₂tēr tā́m swóm-kʷe gʷéru h₁pónts só tā́m gʷémt. nu h₂ŕ̥tḱos tóm kʷéḱt h₂epó-kʷe léytt. nu séh₂ méwdt.
english: The daughter was working in the field. Then a bear came out from the trees. She was afraid, and she cried out. Her brother heard her, and seizing his spear, he came to her. The bear caught sight of him and went away. Then she rejoiced.

english: The man put the bronze in the fire. Then the bronze melted. Then, seizing it, he kept hitting it. He made a spear, and it was pointed. Then a stranger came and bought it. He gave wheat in exchange.

pie: kʷór yéh₂si? h₃rēǵés dʰéh₁mn̥ yéh₂mi. kʷíd bʰéresi? bʰéroh₂ h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m. h₁éymn̥ dl̥h₁gʰóm h₁ésti. ḱóm bʰéh₂omes. kʷís h₃rḗǵs h₁ésti? méǵh₂ ḱléwos h₃rēǵéy h₁ésti tósyo-kʷe h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm h₁ésti.
english: 'Where are you going?' 'I am going to the king's house.' 'What are you carrying?' 'I am carrying wool.' 'The road is long. Let us speak together.' 'Who is the king?' 'The king has great fame, and his name is known.'

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.
